content: Spirulina, also known as blue-green algae, has specific dosing recommendations based on its intended use. For general supplementation, a dose of 1 gram taken orally once daily for 12 days is suggested. Alternatively, 1500 mg of Super Blue-Green Algae (SBGA) capsules can be used as a source of protein, iron, and B vitamins. Spirulina has been found to be effective as a source of protein and iron, although it is relatively expensive when compared to traditional food sources on a gram-for-gram basis. It is likely effective for the treatment of oral leukoplakia and for increasing energy and metabolism. However, it is possibly ineffective as a source of vitamin B12 or as a weight-loss aid. Potential adverse effects associated with Spirulina include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, hepatotoxicity, shock, and hypersensitivity reactions. Contamination with microcystins, a toxic compound, is a concern. Spirulina is contraindicated in individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU). Regarding pregnancy and lactation, there is no specific categorization available (Pregnancy Category: N/A; Lactation: N/A). However, it is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
